protocol: PRE-REGISTER AND FREEZE. Before the final runs, write down (in the repo, dated) the primary endpoint (top-1 ACC on the official DermaMNIST test split, 2,005 images, evaluated on the MedMNIST+ 224-px file dermamnist_224.npz, MD5 8974907d8e169bef5f5b96bc506ae45d; 128-px file MD5 2defd784463fa5243564e855ed717de1; 64-px MD5 b70a2f5635c6199aeaa28c31d7202e1f, which matches the local copy at /Users/suharshkumar/Documents/claude/ddp_summer_dummy/run/dermamnist_64.npz), the secondary endpoints (balanced ACC, macro-F1, macro-AUC, melanoma AUROC and operating points, ECE/NLL/Brier), the external endpoint (DermaMNIST-E test, 1,511 images) and the comparison baselines. Freeze the evaluation script (eval.py) and the decision rule (validation-tuned member weights, logit-adjustment tau, 8-view TTA) BEFORE any test inference; every test number in the paper must come from one invocation of eval.py on a saved probability file.

SAVE PROBABILITIES, NOT JUST NUMBERS. For every model/seed/variant, save the full test softmax matrix (2005 x 7, float32) plus the validation matrix (1003 x 7), the un-adjusted and logit-adjusted versions, with and without TTA, as .npz/.csv keyed by official array index AND by image_id (from dermamnist_split_info.csv). Store SHA-256 of each file and of the input data files in a MANIFEST. Release these with the paper (Zenodo). Every table cell must be recomputable from these files by a one-line command.

USE THE BENCHMARK'S OWN METRIC DEFINITIONS. 'ACC' = accuracy_score(y, argmax(p)); 'AUC' = MedMNIST getAUC = unweighted mean over the 7 one-vs-rest roc_auc_score values (macro OvR), see https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MedMNIST/MedMNIST/main/medmnist/evaluator.py. Compute these with medmnist.Evaluator('dermamnist','test') on the saved file so the numbers are definitionally identical to MedMNIST v2 / MedMNIST+ / Abhishek et al. tables; additionally assert the probability matrix shape is exactly (2005, 7) because the Evaluator only checks row count. Report balanced accuracy = mean per-class recall (the ISIC 2018 Task 3 primary metric) and macro-F1 from sklearn with explicit average='macro'.

SEEDS: 3 independent replicates of the FULL pipeline (each seed re-trains all 5 members, re-tunes the averaging weights and tau on validation, then one test pass). Report mean +/- sample std (ddof=1, n=3) exactly as MedMNIST+ does (e.g. DenseNet-121@224 84.74+/-0.51), and list the three per-seed values in the supplement. Seed everything (python, numpy, torch, CUDA, DataLoader workers), set cudnn.deterministic=True / benchmark=False, and record library versions; state that T4 kernels are not bit-reproducible. If compute forbids 15 trainings at 224 px, the acceptable fallback is: 3 seeds for every single-model row, the ensemble reported once per seed-set with bootstrap CIs, and an explicit statement of the compute budget (GPU-hours per row).

CONFIDENCE INTERVALS FROM THE TEST SET: 95% percentile bootstrap over test images (B = 10,000 for ACC/balanced ACC/F1, B = 2,000 for macro-AUC; fixed RNG seed; same resample indices for all models so paired differences can be computed). Because 26% of HAM10000 lesions have >1 image and the official test set contains several images of the same lesion, ALSO report a cluster bootstrap that resamples lesion_ids (via image_id -> lesion_id from HAM10000 metadata) and show it next to the image-level CI. Expected widths: ACC ~ +/-1.6 pp at n = 2,005; balanced ACC is dominated by df (n = 23) and vasc (n = 29), so expect +/-3-4 pp. Keep seed variability (std over 3 seeds) and sampling uncertainty (bootstrap CI) in separate columns; never present one as the other.

PAIRED SIGNIFICANCE VS BASELINES: McNemar's test on the 2,005 paired correct/incorrect indicators of model vs baseline (exact binomial if discordant pairs b+c < 25, otherwise mid-p; report b, c, p, and the paired accuracy difference with its bootstrap CI). Baselines must be re-run by you to obtain per-image predictions: (a) the July EfficientNet-B0@96 (80.00%), (b) the best single member EfficientNet-B1@112 (81.70%), (c) a DenseNet-121@224 re-trained with the MedMNIST+ recipe (3 seeds) as the proxy for the published 84.74% ceiling, (d) optionally ResNet-18@224. A paired test against a number copied from a table is impossible; if you can only compare to published numbers, say so and use non-overlapping CIs with a caveat. Apply Holm-Bonferroni across the baselines and report the uncorrected p as well. Run McNemar either per matched seed (3 tests, all reported) or once on the seed-averaged ensembles, and say which.

CALIBRATION (on the exact probability vector used for the headline decision rule, AND on the plain un-adjusted ensemble): ECE with 15 equal-width confidence bins (Guo et al. 2017), ECE with 15 equal-mass (adaptive) bins (Nixon et al. 2019) to show binning robustness, classwise ECE (Kull et al. 2019) in the supplement, NLL (mean cross-entropy), multiclass Brier score (mean over images of sum over 7 classes of (p_k - y_k)^2; state this definition, some papers divide by K), and a reliability diagram with bin counts. Temperature scaling, if used, is fit on validation only; report pre/post. State explicitly that logit adjustment (tau) and TTA change the probabilities, so calibration is reported for both p_plain and p_adjusted, and that AUC/ECE for the headline model are computed from p_adjusted (or justify otherwise).

PER-CLASS REPORTING: 7x7 confusion matrix (counts, not just percentages); per-class recall (sensitivity), specificity, precision, F1 and OvR AUC with 95% CIs (Wilson for proportions; bootstrap for AUC). Official test class counts to print under the table (computed from the official file): akiec 66, bcc 103, bkl 220, df 23, mel 223, nv 1341, vasc 29 (train: 228/359/769/80/779/4693/99; val: 33/52/110/12/111/671/14). Note the majority-class baseline is 1341/2005 = 66.88% ACC. Add subgroup rows that HAM10000 metadata enables (dx_type = histo vs follow_up/consensus/confocal, i.e. reference-standard quality as CLAIM 2024 asks; source 'dataset' = vidir_modern / vidir_molemax / rosendahl / vienna_dias; sex; age bands; localization) so reviewers see where the model fails.

MELANOMA OPERATING POINTS: treat p(mel) from the same probability matrix as a binary score. Report melanoma-vs-rest AUROC with DeLong 95% CI and average precision; sensitivity at 80 / 90 / 95% specificity and (ISIC 2017 convention, Codella et al. arXiv 1710.05006) specificity at 82 / 89 / 95% sensitivity. Thresholds MUST be chosen on the validation split (111 melanomas) and then applied to the test split; report the achieved test specificity/sensitivity with Wilson CIs (223 test melanomas -> a sensitivity of 0.80 has a CI of roughly +/-5 pp). Also report melanoma sensitivity/specificity implied by the 7-class argmax rule. Repeat on DermaMNIST-E test (171 melanomas among 1,512 ISIC 2018 test images).

LEAKAGE AUDIT OF THE OFFICIAL SPLIT (no retraining needed): download dermamnist_split_info.csv and HAM10000_metadata.csv from https://github.com/kakumarabhishek/Corrected-Skin-Image-Datasets/tree/main/DermaMNIST/DermaMNIST_Analysis (or HAM10000_metadata.tab from Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/DBW86T, 830,428 B, MD5 8f85fb1aa29d80a2797247e434deb79d). Join split_info (split,index,image_id) with the metadata (lesion_id,image_id,dx,...). Verify the mapping before use: (i) map dx -> {akiec:0,bcc:1,bkl:2,df:3,mel:4,nv:5,vasc:6} and assert the per-split label sequence equals <split>_labels in dermamnist.npz for all 10,015 positions (I spot-checked 15 train + 20 test positions through the ISIC Archive API: 35/35 match, including df/akiec/bcc/mel at the right indices); (ii) optionally compare pixels of the official 224 test image at index i with the dermamnist_corrected_224 / dermamnist_extended_224 image of the same image_id (same source JPEG; small MAE for a correct mapping). Then split the official test set into CLEAN (image's lesion_id has no image in train or val, and not one of the 5 fastdup train-test duplicates; this is exactly the 1,227-image DermaMNIST-C test set) and LEAKED (778 images = 38.8%); report every headline metric on both subsets with CIs. A large clean-vs-leaked gap is evidence of lesion memorisation and must be discussed; reviewers will ask for exactly this table given Abhishek et al. (Sci Data 12:196, 2025).

EXTERNAL / LEAKAGE-FREE TEST: evaluate the official-split models unchanged on the DermaMNIST-E test split (1,511 ISIC 2018 Task 3 test images at 224 px). Verify the 'no leakage' premise yourself: the ISIC 2018 test ground truth on Dataverse (ISIC2018_Task3_Test_GroundTruth.tab, 'same format as HAM10000 metadata') and the ISIC API lesion_id field (IL_ ids) allow a zero-overlap check of lesion_ids between the 10,015 HAM10000 images and the 1,512 test images; report the result. Anchor the -E numbers against Abhishek et al. ResNet-18@224 trained on all 10,015 (ACC 0.685+/-0.000, AUC 0.896+/-0.010), the ISIC 2018 leaderboard top balanced accuracy (~0.885, external data allowed; confirm on challenge.isic-archive.com before citing) and the human-reader study on the same 1,511 images (Tschandl et al., Lancet Oncol 2019). Optionally also train the -E protocol itself (train on all 10,015, checkpoint-select on the 193-image val) for a like-for-like row; note the 193-image val has only 21 melanomas, so use it for checkpoint selection only, not for tuning.

LESION-DISJOINT RE-SPLIT (secondary benchmark, clearly labelled): build a 7:1:2 split of all 10,015 images with sklearn StratifiedGroupKFold (groups = lesion_id, stratify on dx), fixed seed, publish the resulting image_id->split CSV, retrain the single best member and the ensemble with the frozen recipe, and report the same metric panel. Also report on DermaMNIST-C using ITS train/val/test (8,215/573/1,227) to compare with Abhishek ResNet-18@224 0.847+/-0.010 and Kadric et al. 0.8490. Never place these numbers in the same column as official-split numbers; Abhishek et al. state explicitly that DermaMNIST and DermaMNIST-C benchmarks should not be compared. State the limitation that HAM10000 has lesion_id but no patient_id, so patient-level grouping is impossible.

RESOLUTION AND INPUT PROVENANCE: state for every row which file was read (28 / 64 / 128 / 224 npz with MD5), the network input size, interpolation used for any resizing, and whether the comparison rows are native-resolution (MedMNIST+) or 28-px-upsampled (MedMNIST v2 '224' rows are 28 -> 224 nearest-neighbour). Note that DermaMNIST-C/-E 224 images were produced by PIL bicubic resize of the 600x450 originals to a 224x224 square (aspect ratio not preserved); check and report whether this matches the MedMNIST+ 224 preprocessing by comparing the same image_id across files, because a preprocessing mismatch is a confound when evaluating official-split models on -E.

REPORTING CHECKLIST: follow CLAIM 2024 (Tejani et al., Radiology: AI 2024, doi:10.1148/ryai.240300) and Metrics Reloaded (Maier-Hein, Reinke et al., Nat Methods 21:195-212, 2024) item by item: dataset provenance and licences (DermaMNIST, HAM10000 and the -C/-E npz files are CC BY-NC 4.0; the -C/-E CSVs CC BY 4.0), exact split sizes, class prevalence, reference standard (dx_type), model selection procedure, all hyper-parameter search ranges and the number of configurations tried, compute budget, seeds, metric definitions with formulas, CIs for every number, failure analysis, and release of code + probabilities + split files. Cite Abhishek et al. 2025, Yang et al. 2023 (MedMNIST v2), Doerrich et al. 2025 (MedMNIST+), Tschandl et al. 2018 (HAM10000), Codella et al. 2019 (ISIC 2018).

leakage_free_sets.name: DermaMNIST-C (corrected, lesion-disjoint re-partition of all 10,015 HAM10000 images; Abhishek, Jain, Hamarneh, Sci Data 12:196, 2025)
leakage_free_sets.how_to_get: Zenodo record https://zenodo.org/records/12739457 (v1.1; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.11101337 always resolves to the latest version; the older record 11101338 holds byte-identical files, same MD5s). Files: dermamnist_corrected_224.npz (1,131,258,316 B, MD5 84920fb70c83b234c295b6f0d4ae2bc0), dermamnist_corrected_28.npz (20,698,236 B, MD5 96e2862980877d45d9cacb5c25de6950), DermaMNIST-C.csv (747,941 B, MD5 1c54bc9f483e97a9d7dbbde076a45900). Direct URL pattern: https://zenodo.org/records/12739457/files/<name>?download=1. The 28-px npz and the CSV are also in the GitHub repo (DermaMNIST/DermaMNIST_Analysis/NPZ_files/ and CSV_files/combined_metadata_corrected-HAM10000_corrected.csv, identical size). Only 28 and 224 exist; there is no 64 or 128 version.
leakage_free_sets.format: Compressed .npz with the MedMNIST key layout: train_images, train_labels, val_images, val_labels, test_images, test_labels. Images uint8 (N, 224, 224, 3) [or (N, 28, 28, 3)], labels uint8 (N, 1) with akiec=0, bcc=1, bkl=2, df=3, mel=4, nv=5, vasc=6 (same as MedMNIST). Load with d = np.load(path); X = d['test_images']; y = d['test_labels'].ravel() (np.load is lazy per key, so reading only the test arrays costs ~185 MB RAM), or install the repo's medmnist_corrected package, copy the npz to ~/.medmnist/ and use flag dermamnist_corrected_224 (class DermaMNIST_Corrected_224). Metadata CSV columns: lesion_id (HAM_0000118 style), image_id (ISIC_0027419), dx, dx_type, age, sex, localization, dataset, split with split in {train, val, test}; within each split the npz array order equals the CSV row order (CreateNPZfromCSV.ipynb iterates rows in file order), and the CSV is grouped by dx, so the npz is ordered by class. Images were produced by PIL bicubic resize of the original 600x450 JPEGs straight to 224x224 (or 28x28); aspect ratio not preserved.
leakage_free_sets.split_sizes: 8,215 train / 573 val / 1,227 test (10,015 total). Construction: every lesion_id present in the original train split had all its val/test images moved to train (giving 8,208/575/1,232), then 7 fastdup-confirmed near-duplicate pairs were moved too (5 train-test, 2 train-val images) giving 8,215/573/1,227. The -C test set is a strict subset of the official 2,005-image test set; -C val is a subset of official val; -C train is a superset of official train. Per-class counts are not printed anywhere in the paper or repo; compute them with pandas groupby(['split','dx']) on DermaMNIST-C.csv and print them in the paper.
leakage_free_sets.caveat: Not comparable to official-split numbers (different train and test sets; the authors say so explicitly), and leakage removal makes published accuracy go UP (ResNet-18@224: 0.754 original vs 0.847+/-0.010 on -C) because the test set shrinks and the train set grows. Two legitimate uses: (1) as the CLEAN subset of the official test set for models trained on the official split (map image_id -> official test index via dermamnist_split_info.csv); (2) as its own benchmark after retraining on -C train/val (compare with Abhishek ResNet-18@224 0.847+/-0.010 and Kadric et al. 2025 0.8490). Licence CC BY-NC 4.0 for npz, CC BY 4.0 for CSV.

The 193-image validation set (21 melanomas) is too small for hyper-parameter tuning. leakage_free_sets.caveat: Numbers on the clean subset, the -C test set or a new lesion-disjoint re-split are NOT comparable with the official-split literature; present them in a separate table as a robustness/leakage analysis. The clean subset is smaller (wider CIs) and has a different class mix (compute and print its per-class counts). The official validation split is itself leaky w.r.t. test (128 shared images), so any 'validation-tuned' component (member weights, tau, TTA choice, temperature) is mildly test-informed; disclose this and show the clean-subset result.

statistics: Headline table format per model row: ACC, balanced ACC, macro-F1, macro-AUC each as mean +/- std over 3 seeds (ddof=1), plus the 95% percentile bootstrap CI (B = 10,000 image resamples; B = 2,000 for AUC) of the seed-averaged ensemble in brackets; per-seed values in the supplement. Also print n_test = 2,005 and the per-class test counts (66/103/220/23/223/1341/29).

Minimum detectable difference: with n = 2,005 and ACC ~0.83 the single-test-set 95% CI half-width is ~1.6 pp, so 82.64% vs the published 84.74% (DenseNet-121@224) is within sampling noise; a claim of superiority at >= 87% needs the paired McNemar p-value and the CI of the paired difference, not just the point estimate.

McNemar (Dietterich 1998; Fagerland et al. 2013 for mid-p): build the 2x2 table of (model correct, baseline correct) over the same 2,005 images; b = baseline-only-correct, c = model-only-correct; exact binomial p if b + c < 25 else mid-p; report b, c, p, delta-ACC with paired bootstrap CI; Holm-Bonferroni across baselines. Requires per-image predictions of the baseline, hence re-run baselines under the frozen protocol.

Cluster (lesion-level) bootstrap for the official test set: resample lesion_ids with replacement and take all their images, because 26% of HAM10000 lesions have multiple images and image-level bootstrap understates variance; report both CIs.

Macro-AUC: mean of 7 one-vs-rest roc_auc_score values (MedMNIST getAUC; equals sklearn roc_auc_score(multi_class='ovr', average='macro')). Do not report 'ovo' or 'weighted' and call it the benchmark AUC. CI by bootstrap. Melanoma-vs-rest AUROC CI by DeLong (1988; fast implementation Sun & Xu 2014) and bootstrap for cross-check.

Per-class metrics with 95% Wilson CIs for recall/specificity/precision; small classes (df 23, vasc 29, akiec 66 in test) have CIs of +/-15-20 pp, which is why balanced accuracy has a +/-3-4 pp CI and should not be over-interpreted at the second decimal.

Melanoma operating points: sensitivity at 80/90/95% specificity and specificity at 82/89/95% sensitivity (ISIC 2017 convention), thresholds fixed on validation, achieved test values with Wilson CIs; average precision for melanoma; also report the operating point implied by the 7-class argmax rule. 223 melanomas in the official test set, 171 in the ISIC 2018 test set.

Calibration: ECE (15 equal-width bins on max-softmax confidence), adaptive ECE (15 equal-mass bins), classwise ECE, NLL, multiclass Brier (sum over classes, mean over images); reliability diagram; bootstrap CIs for ECE (it is noisy at n = 2,005). Report for p_plain and p_adjusted, with and without TTA, before/after validation-fitted temperature scaling. Prefer proper scoring rules (NLL, Brier) as primary calibration evidence since ECE depends on binning.

Model-selection accounting: report the number of configurations evaluated on validation (members, weights, tau grid, TTA views, temperature) so the reader can judge the optimism of validation-tuned choices; never evaluate any configuration on test more than once per seed.

Seed/variance literature to cite: Bouthillier et al. 2021 (Accounting for variance in ML benchmarks), Picard 2021 (seed selection inflates results); report the std over seeds AND never pick the best seed. Tests on the same test set across many metrics inflate false positives: declare the primary endpoint in advance.

Reporting rules: metric definitions with formulas and sklearn calls in the appendix; every number traceable to a saved probability file and a command; CIs for every number in the main tables; exact data file names and MD5s; software versions; GPU type and total GPU-hours.
pitfalls: Test-set tuning in disguise: choosing members, averaging weights, tau, TTA views, temperature, checkpoints or even the resolution by looking at test metrics. Every such choice must be made on validation with the test file never read until eval.py runs once per seed; keep a log of test evaluations.

Reporting only the best seed, or presenting a single-run result as if it were the mean; or reporting std over seeds for the single models but a one-off ensemble in the same column without saying so. Also conflating bootstrap CI with seed std.

Mixing splits: training on train+val after tuning on val, using val or test images for pretraining or self-supervised warm-up, or using the public ISIC 2018 validation/test ground truth for training when also evaluating on DermaMNIST-E. The official val split also shares 128 images (113 lesions) with test, so heavy validation tuning is mildly test-informed; disclose and show the clean-subset result.

Comparing to the wrong 224 numbers: MedMNIST v2 '224' rows are 28-px images upsampled by nearest neighbour (ResNet-18 75.4%); native 224 rows are MedMNIST+ (ResNet-18 82.33, DenseNet-121 84.74, DINO ViT-B/16 linear probe 84.42). Phase-2 numbers obtained from the 64-px file upsampled to 96-128 are a third regime; state the input file for every row.

Comparing across test sets: official (2,005) vs DermaMNIST-C (1,227, a subset with different class mix) vs DermaMNIST-E (1,511 ISIC 2018 images) vs a custom lesion-disjoint re-split. Abhishek et al. state that DermaMNIST and DermaMNIST-C benchmarks should not be compared, and -C accuracy is HIGHER than the original while -E is lower; never write 'accuracy fell by X after removing leakage' unless the test images are identical.

Treating an unverified preprint as the bar: Wu & Papiez (arXiv 2501.14685, 92.02% DINOv2) is unreviewed and inconsistent with every peer-reviewed table; do not claim or deny SOTA relative to it without reproducing it; cite it with the caveat.

Hidden leakage through pretraining: ISIC 2019 and ISIC 2020 training sets, 'ISIC archive' dumps and dermatology foundation models trained on them (e.g. PanDerm/MONET-style models) CONTAIN all 10,015 HAM10000 images, i.e. the DermaMNIST test set. Only generic pretraining (ImageNet, LVD-142M DINOv2) is admissible; state the pretraining corpus of every backbone.

Label-order bugs when combining files: HAM10000/MedMNIST use alphabetical akiec, bcc, bkl, df, mel, nv, vasc (0..6), but the ISIC 2018 / DermaMNIST-E one-hot columns are MEL, NV, BCC, AKIEC, BKL, DF, VASC; use diag_int, assert class counts after loading, and assert the saved probability matrix is (N, 7) with rows summing to 1.

Wrong AUC: computing AUC on one-hot argmax predictions, using 'ovo' or 'weighted' averaging, or dropping classes; the Evaluator does not check the number of columns, so a transposed or 6-column file silently produces a wrong number.

Accuracy inflated by class imbalance: 66.9% of the test set is nv, so ACC alone is uninformative (SAM linear probe collapses to 66.88% majority class in MedMNIST+). Always pair ACC with balanced ACC and per-class recall, and do not switch decision rules between metrics (e.g. logit-adjusted argmax for balanced ACC but plain argmax for ACC) without reporting both rules for both metrics.

Calibration mistakes: ECE with a different bin count than stated, temperature fitted on test, reporting calibration for un-adjusted probabilities while the decision rule uses adjusted ones, ignoring that TTA and ensembling change calibration, Brier normalised by K without saying so.

Bootstrap mistakes: resampling predictions independently per model (breaks pairing), too few resamples, ignoring lesion clustering, or bootstrapping a seed-averaged number and calling the result 'variance over seeds'.

Paired test against a table: McNemar needs per-image predictions of both systems on the same images; you cannot test against the published 84.74%. Re-train the baseline or use CI overlap with explicit caveats.
Multiple comparisons and metric shopping: many metrics x many baselines x many subsets; declare the primary endpoint and correct the p-values.
Non-reproducible 'seeds': cudnn benchmark mode, nondeterministic kernels, unpinned library versions, Colab image drift; log everything and state what remains nondeterministic.

Data-provenance gaps: not reporting file names/MD5s (dermamnist.npz 0744692d...; _64 b70a2f56...; _128 2defd784...; _224 8974907d...; corrected/extended MD5s as listed), Zenodo version (12739457 vs 11101338), or the easter-egg removal (1,511 not 1,512).

Preprocessing confounds: DermaMNIST-C/-E 224-px images are PIL bicubic squashes of 600x450 originals; the MedMNIST+ 224 pipeline may differ. Evaluating an official-split model on -E without checking this mixes distribution shift with resize shift.

Licence and ethics items reviewers check: HAM10000, DermaMNIST and the -C/-E npz files are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); cite Tschandl 2018, Yang 2023, Doerrich 2025, Abhishek 2025, Codella 2019; no new ethics approval needed but say so.

Claims that exceed the evidence: 'clinically useful', 'dermatologist-level' or 'robust' are not supported by a 2,005-image internal test; the only external evidence is the ISIC 2018 test (DermaMNIST-E) and even that shares acquisition sources for 1,196 of 1,512 images.

Papers on HAM10000 have been sunk by exactly these issues: random image-level splits yielding 90%+ accuracies that collapse under lesion-level splits (documented by Abhishek et al. for DermaMNIST and Fitzpatrick17k), 'patient-level split' claims for a dataset with no patient IDs, citing 28-px-upsampled MedMNIST '224' baselines as native 224, and reporting the best of many seeds. Pre-empt each explicitly in the paper's Methods and Limitations.
